summary: Polish the automation screens (#1352): motion tokens --motion-instant/fast/base/slow, --motion-fade, --motion-flash and --ease-out/in/standard in the SDK stylesheet (0 under prefers-reduced-motion, an opacity change keeps at most 80 ms), Tailwind duration-instant|fast|base|slow and ease-out|in|standard, shared classes iota-press, iota-enter, iota-fade-in, iota-exit, iota-row-exit, iota-row-return, iota-flash, iota-reveal, iota-click and iota-focus-ring, and @iota-uz/sdk/solid-ui motionMs, prefersReducedMotion, createPresence and createFlash. The graph editor answers each action in motion: handle hover and press, rewiring dims the old edge, a valid target lights up, a new edge flashes, a missed release pulls back into its handle, a dragged card lifts and lands on the grid, Tidy and its undo glide with the edges following, the palette, menus, node panel and Validation leave by their reverse animation and are inert meanwhile, the long-press ring fills; the run view lights the taken path in step order and animates the edge of a waiting step; the automations pages, Integrations, the task inbox and notification channels take every timing from the tokens. The editor takes an optional controlled dock (dock / onDock; dockParam and parseDock give its URL form) and the automations page keeps the open Dry run or Test node dock in the URL. The canvas benchmark also measures the Tidy glide. A test fails on any duration or curve outside the tokens on these screens.
